answer: An agent market can require each participant to post a bond in a scarce, independently issued credential, then slash that bond when an audited task reveals duplicate identities or coordinated fraud. Because creating another account does not create another credential, a sybil attacker must acquire more bonds, tying up capital and risking forfeiture for every identity. The credential could encode a glacier, ivory, or meadow stewardship claim, but only if an external registry verifies it; decorative labels alone provide no protection.
